name: PDEM
definition_zh: 通过概率密度随动力过程的演化研究随机响应分布的方法。
definition_en: A method that tracks the evolution of probability density in stochastic dynamical systems using probability conservation.
usage_overview: 基于概率守恒，利用动力响应轨迹将随机输入的概率信息传递到随时间变化的响应概率密度，连接确定性动力计算与随机响应评价。在车辆—轨道等耦合系统中，用于分析随机激励下的响应分布，也用作其他随机分析方法的比较基准。

Finally, a probability density evolution method (PDEM) is introduced to solve the probabilistic transmission issue between track random irregularities and dynamic responses.
PDEM is a newly developed method applied to capture the probabilistic features, particu-larly PDF, of the linear or nonlinear dynamic system through the trajectories of dynamic responses [30].
By post-processing the responses of dynamic indices using PDEM, the probability density surface against time can be accessed.

Finally, a probability density evolution method (PDEM) is introduced to solve the probabilistic transmission issues between track irregularity sets and dynamic responses of vehicle–track coupled systems.
For readers interested in PDEM, the details can be consulted to a serial of research work by Li and Chen [31–33].

The probability density evolution method (PDEM) proposed by Li and Chen [23] is capable of capturing the instantaneous probability transmission, which has provided new perspectives to tackle stochastic vibration based issues.

The mean and standard deviation (Std. D) of the response as well as its probability density function (PDF) evolution can be acquired by PDEM and vehicle-track dynamic model with relatively high efficiency.
Though PDEM has arrived at almost the same accuracy level as MCS, the computational efficiency has been greatly improved.
In this section, the proposed VTCM–TIPM–PDEM model will be applied to evaluate the dynamic reliability of the dynamic performance of a railway vehicle.
The mean value and the standard deviation of track slab acceleration computed by the PDEM and MCM, respectively, are compared as shown in Figure 8.
Note that 1500 sampling cases are calculated in the MCM simulation, while the PDEM analysis is much more efficient with 100 representative samples.

Except for the random simulation of system geometric and parametric excitations and the dynamic model for train–track interaction, a PDEM with probability dissipation considered is introduced to achieve the probabilistic transmission between the system inputs and response outputs.

Apart from the validations, several conclusions can be drawn accordingly (1) The random sample selections can be effectively applied to investigate the probability distribution and amplitude–frequency characteristics of system responses by the combination of the train–track interaction model and PDEM.
